text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces decided to become a single political party and form a coalition for early parliamentary elections with the ethnic Turk Movement for Rights and Freedoms and the People's Union.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to raise sharply maximum fuel prices today in line with the drastic fall of the lev. @
-- Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski is expected to cut by nearly one third the adminstrative staff at the Council of Ministers.

-- The Socialist Party leader Georgi Parvanov will head the socialist pre-election headquarters, the leadership of the party decided. Former premier Zhan Videnov and his closest associates were not likely to be put on the draft election lists for deputies in the future parliament, socialists said.

-- Bulgaria's former interior minister and prominent socialist Nikolai Dobrev said he was fully supporting urgent measures by the interim cabinet to beef up border control in order to prevent speculative exports of fuel.
-- Bulgaria's trade unions said they were ready for a social peace pact with the caretaker government of Stefan Sofianski and would not stage any strikes or protests during its mandate.
-- President Petar Stoyanov is expected to appoint a Central Electoral Commission today which is to carry out early general election on April 19. @

-- Former ministers, deputy ministers and advisors from the former Socialist cabinet of Zhan Videnov and members of their families had their passports confiscated to prevent siphoning of money and taking abroad vital documents, interim premier Stefan Sofianski said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
